text:
Alex (Head of Platform): FYI launching a small pilot for Just-In-Time Operator Access (JITA) for Private/VPC customers. Goal: let Redwood engineers request time-limited privileged access to customer clusters using customer-controlled approval flows and full auditability. Pilot is opt-in, invite-only (7 customers). Pilot docs + signup: https://intranet.redwood/jita-pilot :satellite:

Priya (Security): Summary: JITA sessions are ephemeral, RBAC-Scoped, and require customer approval via signed webhook or a customer-managed approval UI. We emit an auditable session bundle (operator identity, actions, timestamps, signed by our KMS). Telemetry for pilot = session metadata, action verbs, and success/failure flags only. No model or customer payloads are captured. Retention for audit bundles during pilot: 90 days. Compliance writeup: https://intranet.redwood/security/jita-audit :lock:

Omar (Infra): Tech notes: implementation uses short-lived certificates (30m default), automatic session termination, and per-session signed attestation blobs. Example customer policy snippet we propose to provide: 
```yaml
jita_policy:
  max_session_minutes: 30
  approval_mode: webhook # webhook | ui
  maintenance_window_required: true
  default_maintenance_window: "Sat 00:00-02:00 UTC"
```
Ops will require a weekly maintenance window (2 hours) for non-emergency JITA actions so we can schedule low-impact operations. Emergency flows remain available but require explicit customer-signed consent.

Leanne (Legal): Legal note: customers must sign a short addendum to enable JITA remote operator access. Addendum will describe scope of access, data handling, and audit rights. For customers who decline, we will offer manual support with longer SLAs. I'll circulate the addendum draft and a carveout template by EOD Tuesday.

Nina (CS): I'll prepare customer outreach templates and a one-page FAQ that explains: what JITA is, how approvals work, telem/retention, rollback expectations, and how to opt-out. Draft blurb for pilots: "By opting into JITA you enable faster troubleshooting with time-limited, auditable operator sessions. If you decline, remediation will be performed via documented manual procedures and may take longer."

deploy-bot: Scheduling: jita-preview v0.1 -> infra-staging at 2098765800

Priya (Security): Action items: add JITA pilot to SOC tracker, publish attestation schema, and confirm HSM signing flow. Customers requiring zero remote admin must sign the "no-remote-admin" waiver; those accounts will be excluded from JITA invites.

Omar (Infra): Rollout plan: invite 7 pilot accounts -> run 2 supervised sessions per account -> collect audit bundles + post-session verification -> week 3 consolidate findings and update GA checklist. Automatic rollback rules apply to any session that triggers >8% node error or >10s median latency increase within 10m.

Alex (Head of Platform): Policy note: if JITA moves to GA we'll require explicit written consent for managed Private support customers to allow temporary operator access. We'll give a 60-day notice before making consent a gating condition for proactive support. If you have objections to the 60-day notice or the 2-hour maintenance window requirement, please reply here by EOD Wednesday. Otherwise we'll finalize pilot invites tomorrow and start customer outreach. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
